question: Do heatwave signals (NASA POWER daily Tmax/T2M) improve monthly hydropower-shortfall warnings?
design: Future-detector v2 back-test re-run with and without heat features: train target months <= 2020, test 2021-01..2025-12, logistic regression (chosen on a 2018-2020 validation split), climatology and persistence baselines, 300-sample block bootstrap over test months, P >= 0.4 alert rule fixed in advance.

features.hw_days: days in the month inside a heatwave (Tmax above the 1991-2020 calendar-day 90th percentile, +-7-day window, for >= 3 consecutive days), averaged over the unit's points
features.hw_l1/hw_l2/hw_3m: heatwave days 1 and 2 months before the issue month, and the 3-month sum
features.tx_z (+_l1, _l2, 3): monthly mean Tmax anomaly, z vs 1991-2020 same calendar month, its lags and 3-month mean
features.cdd_z (+3): cooling degree days (base 18 C) z vs 1991-2020, and 3-month mean
features.issue_time: all heat features use days up to the end of the issue month only

labels.short: generation below the unit's training-year 20th percentile for that calendar month
labels.short_adj: capacity-corrected: ratio to the median of the same month in the previous 5 years, below the training 20th percentile

verdict: Heat adds no pooled skill: hydro history + heat vs hydro history AUC-PR x1.006 [90% 1.001-1.011] at 1 month, x0.99 at 3, x0.985 [0.977-0.997] at 6; full model + heat vs full x1.00 / x0.99 / x0.98; Brier skill unchanged.
Summer target months (Jun-Sep NH, Dec-Mar SH): x1.01 at 1 month, worse at 3-6 months (x0.94-0.98, intervals below 1).

Only hint: snow/glacier-fed units in summer, hydro + heat x1.03-1.07 at 1-3 months on the capacity-corrected label (intervals above 1), but not on the raw label beyond 1 month and nothing on top of the full model. Suggestive only.

Sichuan 2022 still missed. August 2022 had 10 heatwave days (Tmax +1.7 sd), but Ember provincial monthly hydro for August is near normal (-1.7% YoY); only September (-22% YoY) is a shortfall, on the capacity-corrected label. September P at 1 month: full + heat 0.03, heat only 0.29 (below the 0.4 rule). National China not flagged earlier.

Why: the heatwave and the generation drop arrived in the same 4-6 weeks, so monthly heat known at issue time cannot lead it; elsewhere heat is redundant with recent generation. Heat-only alerts (P >= 0.4) are right 35-39% of the time vs a 29-30% base rate.
Recommendation: do not add monthly heat features to the shortfall model. Flash heat-droughts need sub-monthly generation/inflow data and heat forecasts (S2S Tmax), not lagged monthly heat.

notes: Produced by the future-detector back-test (separate repo), not by this pipeline; it does not change any existing Patronus file or forecast.

Units: 53 Ember countries, Brazil national + 4 ONS subsystems, 10 US states (EIA), Kariba lake level (scored separately), plus Sichuan (CHN-SC) from Ember China provincial monthly generation. 68 generation units in the pooled score.
Heat data: NASA POWER daily point API (T2M_MAX, T2M), 1990-01-01..2026-10-31, up to 12 points per unit box, 330 points, 0 failed requests. Climatologies (p90 thresholds, z-scores) use 1991-2020 only.

Some inputs of the future-detector models have no id in meta.json and so are not listed in sources: EIA state hydro (bulk ELEC.zip), NOAA CPC soil moisture, CSR and JPL GRACE mascons, GPM IMERG V07, GRACE-DA (GRACEDADM), SMAP L4. The GRACE inputs are not GFZ GravIS (gravis).
Unit codes inside the back-test are future-detector codes (e.g. BRA_SE, US_WA); Sichuan is written as CHN-SC to match countries.json.

Sichuan has only 5 training years (2016-2020) and grew >20 GW of hydro, so its raw-label threshold rarely fires; the monthly series does not show the two-week August 2022 crisis (same finding as generation_backtest.json).
Data latency is ignored (month t assumed known at the end of month t), as in the earlier back-test. Probabilities are not recalibrated.

Snow/glacier-fed subset was hand-picked before scoring: CHE, AUT, NOR, SWE, ISL, KGZ, TJK, PAK, GEO, CAN, NZL, US_WA, US_OR, US_ID, US_MT, US_CA, US_AZ, CHN_SC. Many subsets were compared on one 2021-2025 test period, so intervals just above 1 are weak evidence.
bss_vs_climatology is 1 - Brier/Brier(climatology); auc_pr_ratio intervals are 90% block-bootstrap (300 resamples over test months).
